summary: The Czech Republic eased renewable permitting in 2023 and has a legal framework for bankable long-term PPAs, though the corporate PPA market is still small. Auctions for wind support were legislated, and profits can be repatriated.

access.reason: An auction framework for wind support has been adopted, but the sources did not confirm auctions running.

ownership.reason: The crown is fully convertible, and profits can be repatriated.

build.reason: Permitting was eased in 2023, but grid operators face growing pressure from new connections.

direction.reason: The 2023 Lex RES I amendments simplify permits and licences.

access.reason: The legal framework allows bankable long-term PPAs, but the market is less developed than elsewhere, with the first large PPA in 2021.

terms.reason: Longer-term price fixing is legally available.

build.reason: Plants up to 50 kW no longer need a generation licence.

direction.reason: Permitting has been simplified and PPAs are expected to grow.

events.title: Lex RES I eases licensing and permits for renewable plants

sources.title: Renewable energy in the Czech Republic
Czech Republic Country Commercial Guide, trade financing

gaps: Rule stability, including the 2011 solar levy and later changes, and the status of wind auctions were not established from the sources reviewed.
